title: test-0114-SOC-HIS-FRENCHREV
passage: The French Revolution was a complex struggle for power that reshaped society. Before 1789, the social structure was divided into three estates, where only the Third Estate paid taxes to the state, while the First and Second Estates enjoyed privileges. The subsistence crisis was not merely a result of the King’s choices, but a combination of bad harvests and rising bread prices that crippled the poor. When the Estates General met, the King insisted that each estate cast only one collective vote, rather than allowing every individual representative to vote separately. This unfair system sparked outrage. Later, the National Assembly defined 'active citizens' as men above 25 who paid taxes equal to at least three days of a laborer’s wage, excluding women and poorer men from voting. Even as revolutionary ideals spread, women remained excluded from political rights, and slavery in French colonies was not permanently abolished until much later, as the 1794 decree was eventually overturned by Napoleon. Furthermore, the Bastille, which was stormed by the people, held only seven prisoners at the time, not hundreds as rumors suggested. The Revolution was a battle for systemic change, not just a series of riots or simple acts of rebellion.
summary: Before 1789, the social structure was divided into three estates: the First and Second Estates enjoyed privileges, and the Third Estate paid taxes. When the Estates General met, the King insisted that each estate cast only one collective vote, rather than allowing every individual representative to vote separately.
